reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio SAT5-SAT6 campus discloses 33 MW of IT capacity and 175,000 square feet of technical space, but publishes nothing about grid interconnection, power source, or whether that capacity is allocated, so its role in AI scaling remains unmeasurable.

The 33 MW ranks sixth among the nineteen Texas facilities that publish power capacity, 6.9% of the state's disclosed 475 MW total, but that rank reflects disclosure rather than market position because 114 of 133 mapped Texas facilities publish no capacity figure. The certifications listed, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, TIA-942, and HITRUST, are hygiene requirements for enterprise and regulated customers, not specialized markers for AI.

What the data does not show matters more for compute and power. There is no published grid interconnection, power source, or contract status for the 33 MW, so it cannot be counted as available AI capacity. Without actual GPU deployment, rack density, or workload mix, the campus cannot be assessed as a binding constraint on AI scaling, and the operator's specification page does not address those questions.
